learningObjective: Identify the defining properties of a dataflow / computational graph as used by deep learning compilers.
stem: In the standard formulation of a deep-learning computational graph (dataflow graph), which of the following are true properties? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Every edge in the graph is required to be materialized in memory as an intermediate tensor; a compiler that fuses ops must add explicit memory nodes on the fused edge.
Each node's output shape and dtype are typically inferred (shape inference / type inference) from the node's operator and its input shape/dtype; this is a routine graph-level analysis.
Nodes represent operations and edges represent tensor values flowing from a producer to one or more consumers; the graph is a directed graph.
The graph is usually acyclic for a single forward pass (a DAG), which makes topological order well-defined and enables straightforward scheduling and dataflow analysis.

explanation: A dataflow graph is directed (A); a forward pass in a feedforward net is a DAG (B), enabling topological scheduling; and each node's output shape/dtype is normally inferred from operator semantics and input types (D). Option C is wrong: whether an edge is materialized in memory is a codegen/scheduling decision. Fused kernels represent a shared iteration space where intermediates live in registers, not memory — no explicit memory nodes need to be added to the graph.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: materialization is a scheduling choice, not a property of the graph.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: DAG structure for forward passes is standard.

assumptions: The graph represents a single forward pass over a feedforward model; training graphs with backward passes are still DAGs after autograd generates the joint graph.
The framework provides shape/type inference for its ops.
nonImplications: Does not imply all deep-learning workloads produce DAGs; graphs with control flow can require additional constructs (control edges, sub-graphs).
Does not imply shape inference always succeeds; dynamic shapes can leave dims symbolic or unknown.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses graph edges with runtime memory allocation.
